modelNotes: Each remaining match is simulated 20,000 times from a Poisson goals model: team attack and defence ratings plus home advantage, fitted on this season with a 240-day half-life.

FixtureDownload has no Ligue 2 season before 2026-27, so every team, promoted or relegated, started this season from the same average rating, and ratings are held closer to it than usual (backtests without a previous season scored better that way).

Every simulated season also lets team strength drift (more when more of the season is left), because form, injuries and transfers change teams; without it, early-season odds were overconfident in backtests.

Teams level on points are ranked by goal difference, then head-to-head points, then head-to-head goal difference (once they have met home and away), then overall goals scored, then wins, then away wins; simulated seasons separate them by goal difference, then goals scored.

Backtested on 2025-26 in five leagues: match predictions score 0.20-0.21 (ranked probability score) against 0.22-0.23 for home/draw/away base rates; season odds were calibrated on 18 league-seasons since 2022-23.

There is no earlier Ligue 2 season in the feed to backtest on. With the previous season removed, eight other leagues' 2023-24 to 2025-26 week-ahead predictions scored 0.194-0.222 (ranked probability score) against 0.229-0.235 for home/draw/away base rates, 0.002-0.008 worse than with it. This season's first 63 Ligue 2 matches scored 0.234 against 0.221 for base rates, so treat early match predictions with care.
Away wins are the last tiebreak step modelled; the league then compares disciplinary points, which the feed does not have, and the table falls back to club names.
